questions.prompt: InfoNCE, N=2, identical orthogonal views z=(1,0),(0,1), tau=0.5. What is the loss? (decimal, tolerance 0.001)
One anchor in a batch of 5: positive similarity 0.9, four negatives with similarity 0.3, tau=0.2. What is this anchor's loss? (decimal, tolerance 0.001)
Collapse loss for batch size 1024? (decimal, tolerance 0.001)
InfoNCE bound I ≥ log N − L. With N=128 and measured L=1.2 nats, what lower bound on mutual information (nats)? (decimal, tolerance 0.01)
A contrastive run's loss stays at 6.93 for batch size 1024 from the first epoch on. What is the most likely cause?
options: The learning rate is too small for the loss change to be measurable
The model is perfectly trained, so the loss has reached its minimum value
The temperature is too high for this batch, which flattens the logits
The encoder has collapsed to a constant output (ln 1024 = 6.93)
questions.explanation: ln(1024)=6.93 is exactly the all-equal-logits value.

questions.prompt: An image has 196 patches and the masking ratio is 75%. How many patches does the encoder see (unmasked)? (integer, tolerance 0.01)
Why does BERT replace some selected tokens with random tokens or leave them unchanged rather than always using the mask symbol?
options: It prevents the vocabulary from growing as new tokens appear in the corpus text over time
The mask symbol never appears in fine-tuning, so always using it causes a train/test mismatch
Random tokens make the training loss smaller, so the model learns much faster overall
It speeds up the softmax over the vocabulary by shrinking the output layer size a lot
questions.explanation: The 80/10/10 rule keeps representations of every token useful.

questions.prompt: Which augmentation is most likely label-destroying for left-turn vs right-turn recognition from a forward camera?
options: Small brightness change
Slight Gaussian blur
Horizontal flip
Small random crop
questions.explanation: A horizontal flip swaps left and right, which is the label.

questions.prompt: A candidate augmentation keeps the downstream label in 87 of 120 probe signals. What is the preserved fraction? (decimal, tolerance 0.005)
questions.explanation: 87/120=0.725: far from 1, so not a safe augmentation for this label.

questions.prompt: Batches are built from random frames of a single 10-minute robot video. What is the main risk for in-batch negatives?
options: Positives become negatives of themselves, which zeroes the contrastive loss
Frames are too different from each other, so negatives are trivially easy
Near-duplicate frames from the same scene are treated as negatives (false negatives)
The batch is too small to compute a softmax over the similarities
questions.explanation: Adjacent frames show the same content, so pushing them apart harms the representation.

questions.prompt: Describe a protocol to decide whether an augmentation set is safe before spending GPU hours on pretraining.
rubric: Measure label preservation (preserved fraction) of each augmentation on a labelled probe set.
Run a short pretraining plus linear probe versus raw baseline across several seeds, ablating one augmentation at a time.
Define a falsifier (e.g. no gain over raw features, or collapse/shortcut signs) before running.

questions.prompt: Sketch the code (or pseudocode) for the InfoNCE loss with a batch of two-view embeddings, including numerical stability and the shape of the similarity matrix.
rubric: Normalize embeddings, compute an N×N cosine matrix between view 1 and view 2, divide by tau.
Use log-sum-exp (subtract the row max) and take the diagonal as the positive: loss = mean(logsumexp(row) − diag).
Tests: identical orthogonal pairs give log(1+e^(-1/tau)); collapse gives log N.

questions.prompt: A SimCLR-style batch has 128 images, so each anchor is classified among 2*128 - 1 = 255 candidates (one positive, 254 negatives). The measured loss is 2.0 nats. What lower bound log(255) - loss on the mutual information does this give, in nats? (decimal, tolerance 0.01)
questions.explanation: The InfoNCE bound is I >= log(N_candidates) - L. With 255 candidates, ln 255 = 5.5413, so the bound is 5.5413 - 2.0 = 3.5413 nats. The bound can never exceed ln 255 = 5.54 nats whatever the loss.

questions.prompt: One anchor, four candidates with similarities (0.8, 0.1, 0.1, 0.7) where the first is the positive, temperature tau = 0.1. What is d(loss)/d(similarity of the 0.7 negative)? (decimal, tolerance 0.01)
questions.explanation: d loss / d s_ij = (p_ij - delta_ij)/tau. Logits are (8, 1, 1, 7); softmax weights are (0.73009, 0.00067, 0.00067, 0.26858). For the 0.7 negative the derivative is 0.26858/0.1 = 2.6858. The two easy negatives get only 0.0067 each, a ratio of e^6 = 403.

questions.prompt: In SimCLR, why is composing random cropping with colour distortion much better than random cropping alone?
options: Crops of the same image share a similar colour histogram, so the network can match views by colour statistics instead of learning object structure
Colour distortion makes the images smaller, which lets the batch contain more negative examples
Cropping alone changes the label of the image, and colour distortion restores it
Colour distortion removes the need for a temperature parameter in the loss
questions.explanation: Random crops of one image tend to have the same colour distribution, and colour histograms alone can identify images, so the contrastive task has a shortcut. Colour distortion removes the shortcut; the pretext task becomes harder but the representation improves (Chen et al., SimCLR, section 3). The other options are not mechanisms of the method: image size does not change the number of negatives, crops do not change labels in the standard setting, and the temperature is still needed.
